clue.text: Pyramid goes like this, but not completely

definitions.text: Pyramid goes like this, but not completely

parts.words: Pyramid goes like this, but not completely
parts.note: a pyramid's sides rise until they meet at the apex, so its shape describes a phrase meaning 'partly, to some extent'

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a pyramid is built, and admits it is only partly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the pyramid's shape literally and also describes the idiom: something true only in part.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means partly or to a limited degree, and a pyramid literally rises to its apex.

clue.text: National of this country is to spit on Scotsman

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: the Times is a British paper, so 'this country' is the UK
to spit is to rain lightly
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name in crosswords

explanation.surface: A citizen of some nation is about to spit on a man from Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country; this one belongs to Ukraine.

clue.text: Rwandan sweetheart is vocal

indicators.note: something vocal is spoken out loud, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: tootsie is an affectionate term for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone's darling from Rwanda talks a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are one of the main ethnic groups of Rwanda, so a Rwandan may be one.

clue.text: After a time, turtles engaged in confrontation

indicators.note: the turtles come after 'a time' in the answer

parts.note: loggerheads are a species of large sea turtle

explanation.surface: After a while, some turtles began fighting each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the turtles follow A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in serious dispute or quarrelling is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: Police have forgotten account

parts.note: something forgotten belongs to the past, so it is old
a bill is an account of money owed

explanation.surface: The police have lost track of an account.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bill is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for the police force, as in 'watch out, it's the cops'.

clue.text: Book to see composer

parts.note: a novel is a book
lo is an old word for 'see!' or 'behold'

explanation.surface: Get a book so you can see a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh songwriter and composer of musicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a Welsh songwriter, an example of a composer.

clue.text: Sculpture broken

definitions.meaning: slang for damaged beyond use, or out of money

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a head-and-shoulders statue, and slang for wrecked or not working.

clue.text: Red Cross Knight's bride hit 13? Just the opposite

parts.note: in Spenser's Faerie Queene, Una marries the Redcrosse Knight
to bash is to hit

explanation.surface: The Red Cross Knight's bride struck someone who was uneasy, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is ILL AT EASE; the answer means the opposite, so 13 points to the definition and is not a piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Not embarrassed and self-assured, the reverse of being uncomfortable and on edge.

clue.text: Subject to horrific experience, my eyes have been opened

annotationWithheld.why: Subject to horrific experience, my eyes have been opened: no sound parse of the wordplay found for THEME (possibly the horror film Them! plus E, but 'my eyes have been opened' does not give E cleanly)
annotationWithheld.clue: Subject to horrific experience, my eyes have been opened

clue.text: Disconcerted, let dart go astray

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of their order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A darts player is upset when a dart goes wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rattled means flustered or unsettled, a synonym for disconcerted.

clue.text: A verb — it can be translated as tremble

indicators.note: translating changes the form of the words, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A language note says a certain verb can be rendered as 'tremble'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be translated' rearranges A VERB IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to shake or quiver, the same as to tremble.

clue.text: Two-tone flower providing ingredients for omelette

definitions.meaning: a name for toadflax and other plants whose flowers are yellow and pale cream
the fat and the main ingredient of an omelette

explanation.definitionFit: A folk name for yellow-and-cream flowers such as toadflax, and literally two things you cook an omelette with.

clue.text: Here in Brittany's no good: it's dangerous on the roads

parts.note: ici is French for 'here', the language of Brittany

explanation.surface: In Brittany this place is no good, because the roads are dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the thing that is dangerous: ice forming on the road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice forming on a road makes driving hazardous, so it is a danger on the roads.

clue.text: On edge, I will answer kid

parts.note: contracted, I will is I'll
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A nervous person promises to answer when teased.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is being nervous and uncomfortable, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Naked light, one theatre put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre switches off its light, perhaps for a nude scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means wearing no clothes at all, i.e. nude.

clue.text: Go off musical about old renegades

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour

indicators.note: the musical goes about, i.e. around, the abbreviation for old

parts.note: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A musical about old renegades starts to go sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Turncoats change sides, which is exactly what renegades do.

clue.text: Colour of ball you're kicking about

indicators.note: a ball kicked about is knocked in all directions, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks what colour the ball is that you are kicking around.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep bright shade, an example of a colour.

clue.text: Why don't trawlers work on a bearing of 315 degrees?

definitions.text: Why don't trawlers work on a bearing of 315 degrees?

parts.words: Why don't trawlers work on a bearing of 315 degrees?
parts.note: 315 degrees is the compass direction between north and west; the trawler question suggests the gale from that quarter that keeps fishing boats in port

explanation.surface: Someone asks why fishing boats do not sail on one particular compass heading.
explanation.walkthrough: The question hints at the stormy nor'wester; the compass bearing gives the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearing of 315 degrees points midway between north and west on the compass.

clue.text: For instance, test papers looked easy at first sight

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: only the first letter of each of the next three words is seen

explanation.surface: For instance, the exam papers looked easy when first seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first sight' takes the first letters P, L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is an instance of something, one case standing for the type.

clue.text: Sight a parrot in biblical book

indicators.note: A and the parrot are put inside the book's abbreviation

parts.note: Tim is short for Timothy, two books of the New Testament
the kea is a New Zealand parrot

explanation.surface: A parrot can be seen in a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To sight a gun is to point it at the target, the same as aiming it.

clue.text: Cloth — pedlar robbed of half by a footballer

indicators.note: the pedlar loses the back half of his letters

parts.note: a huckster is a pedlar or hawker
a back is a defensive football player

explanation.surface: A pedlar loses half his cloth to a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'robbed of half' removes STER, leaving HUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Huckaback is a coarse linen or cotton fabric used for towels, a type of cloth.

clue.text: He had, say, turned up to equivocate

parts.note: he had shortens to he'd

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, means 'say'

explanation.surface: He had, let's say, turned up only to dodge the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads EG upwards as GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to avoid committing yourself, which is what equivocating means.

clue.text: Old Nick was around

indicators.note: turned around, the word is read backwards

parts.note: 'lived' can mean 'was', as in 'was alive'

explanation.surface: Old Nick was hanging around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns LIVED into DEVIL. Old Nick is a traditional nickname for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional English nickname for Satan.

clue.text: As a composer, I would speed things up

definitions.text: As a composer, I would speed things up

parts.words: As a composer, I would speed things up
parts.note: the composer's name read backwards says 'I'd rev', i.e. I would speed up

explanation.surface: A composer explains that he likes a brisk tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's name read backwards is I'D REV.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Stops drafts

definitions.meaning: a vehicle halting at the kerb
prepares a document or plan in writing

explanation.definitionFit: A car pulls in and halts; a lawyer prepares a contract in written form.

clue.text: Soothsayer's month by the river

indicators.note: the river is placed beside the month

parts.note: Aug is short for August
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A fortune teller's month spent beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman soothsayer, so augural means belonging to a soothsayer.

clue.text: Tom's friend and playing partner

definitions.meaning: in Tom Brown's Schooldays, Tom's best friend at Rugby School is called ...
in bridge, the player sitting opposite West and partnering them

explanation.definitionFit: Tom Brown's schoolfriend is called East, and at bridge the East seat partners the West seat.

clue.text: Like our society, according to the letter

parts.note: per means according to, as in 'per instructions'
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: Our society is described in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'permissive society' was a phrase used about Britain from the 1960s on.
explanation.definitionFit: A society that tolerates almost anything was called the permissive society.
